title: Fattoush
subtitle: Lebanese bread salad with sumac dressing
excerpt: Fattoush is a Levantine salad built around toasted or fried pieces of flatbread that soak up a sharp sumac and lemon dressing. It is a summer salad of ripe tomatoes, crisp leaves, and fresh herbs. The bread is the defining ingredient.
sourceNotes: Fattoush is a Levantine salad originating in the mountainous regions of Lebanon and Syria. The name comes from the Arabic word fatteh, meaning crumbled bread. It was traditionally a way of using stale flatbread, dressed with the sour red spice sumac.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the vegetables and toast the bread separately. Dress and combine just before serving.

content.text: Add the toasted bread at the very last minute before serving -- it softens quickly once dressed. If you want it crispy, serve the bread pieces on the side and let people add their own.

items.prepNote: use 1 tsp sumac plus juice of the lemon for the dressing

content.text: Toast 2 large flatbreads or 2 thick slices of stale bread under the grill or in a dry pan until golden and crisp. Break into rough pieces.
Put the tomatoes, red pepper, spring onion, and parsley in a large bowl.
Whisk the lemon juice, sumac, olive oil, cumin, and salt together in a small bowl.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables. Toss gently to coat.
Add the toasted bread pieces just before serving. Toss once more and serve immediately.

items.cause: Added to the salad too early
items.fix: Always add the bread at the very last minute, or serve it alongside for people to add themselves

items.cause: Tomatoes were very ripe and released their juice
items.fix: Salt the tomatoes 10 minutes ahead and drain, or simply serve the salad as soon as it is dressed
Add a little extra olive oil to balance the acidity

content.text: Fattoush is a staple of the Lebanese meze table and is eaten widely in Syria, Jordan, and Palestine. It is summer food -- made when tomatoes are at their best. The sharp red sumac spice is the defining flavour. It is very similar to the Italian panzanella in concept, suggesting that stale bread salads appear independently across many cultures.
